scope: Independent read-only physical interpretation; static measurements and local diagnostic chord only. No heavy solve, package/source edits, servers or simulators.
conclusion: The rim is a real bearing, but the 11.2 mm lateral bow is an artifact of the selected independent section/collar approximation, not a demonstrated physically necessary lateral bearing. Some separation from the other lead is necessary; this particular detour is not established as necessary.

sourceEvidence.supported: Front-cavity entry into two distinct floor openings. Images were inspected directly.
sourceEvidence.notSupported: No retained loaded vertical-pose image establishes the lateral bow, a fixed exterior collar bearing, equal loaded lead lengths or a hidden connection.

decisiveLocalCounterexample.operation: Replace a 1 mm portion on each side of the unsupported exterior-collar knee by its chord; all remaining points including support and mouth unchanged.
decisiveLocalCounterexample.frontEntry: Unchanged axis-aligned final 21.2 mm to the actual front mouth
decisiveLocalCounterexample.meaning: Published route is not even locally length-minimal when its artificial exterior collar constraint is removed. This diagnostic does not settle height or provide a replacement cache.

solverCause: The first certified orientation is selected after 12 rejected candidates; left-lead -20 degrees is not selected by a length or force-balance objective.
native_mouth_collar pins a point at the entire solid front support plane plus radius and clearance. That conservative exit is treated as a required turning waypoint even when far from any wood.
The lower lead crosses the rim at body y about -10.2 mm, whereas the mouth lies at y=+1 mm. Its imposed section holds that sideward route.

The collar creates an unsupported 90.079-degree turn 21.882 mm from wood. A 1 mm corner cut shortens the path by 0.586759 mm with 20.822 mm certified solid clearance, unchanged mouth/front entry and a passing full-path tube check.

recommendation.preferred: Use the existing certified routes as deterministic initial guesses for a bounded coupled 3D path-shortening/relaxation step. Treat the exterior collar as an initialization aid, not a mandatory free-space bearing.
constraints: Keep the actual native mouth centers and source-backed front entry. Enforce valid entry direction/local bore clearance at the terminal instead of forcing a bend at the global front support plane.
Keep the same fixed world support, pose rotation, native solid, radius and declared rest lengths; permit generated hanging height to re-settle.
Constrain complete segments against the full native solid and every other cord; preserve intentional common support joining and no other contacts.
Use a deterministic iteration budget and fail closed. Retain exact rounded-cache solid, self/interstrand tube, length, reproduction and app-visual gates.
Generated routes only; do not hand-draw the desired straight line or relax collision tolerances.
recommendation.whyFeasible: The existing route provides a collision-free initialization, and the local chord probe proves a strictly shorter nearby feasible path exists without changing any sourced endpoint. A complete corrected solve has not been run.
recommendation.narrowerAlternative: Refine section rotations and choose among passing candidates by a declared path-length/deviation objective, but label this as a visual approximation: it does not remove the unsupported exterior-collar knee and is not the preferred physical correction.

physicalLimitation.meaning: The current settle step makes the longest lead taut; the other visible route is about 347.14 mm despite its 400 mm rest length. The display therefore already omits about 52.86 mm of slack and cannot be claimed as a complete equilibrium of two equal inextensible cords. Preserve dimensions and report this limitation rather than inventing a hidden continuous connection or changing lengths to force a tidy result.
